entries.name: Grey Oyster on Straw
entries.notes: Pasteurised wheat straw or cottonseed hulls colonise in 12-14 days at 23-25 C; shift to 18-20 C and 90 % RH with strong fresh air for fruiting. Grey oysters need high FAE or they develop long stems and small caps. Expect 3-4 flushes at roughly 25-50 % biological efficiency, picking clusters as the cap margins flatten.

provenance.sourceTitle: D.I.Y. FunGuide: Grow Your Own Oyster Mushrooms at Home (UF/IFAS SS662)
provenance.verificationNote: Checked the 24 C / 85 % targets against UF/IFAS, which specifies 20 C and 90 % RH for fruiting initiation; 24 C matches the spawn-run range instead, so the fruiting values were corrected.

entries.name: Shiitake on Sawdust Blocks
entries.notes: Supplemented hardwood sawdust (oak plus 10-20 % bran) colonised at 22-25 C for 3-4 weeks, then browned. Soak or cold-shock the block at 12-15 C for 3-4 hours and fruit at 13-18 C with 85-90 % RH. Pins appear in about a week and harvest follows 7-10 days later; blocks usually give 2-3 flushes.

provenance.sourceTitle: Shiitake Mushroom Production: Fruiting, Harvesting, and Storage (Ohio State University Extension)
provenance.verificationNote: Confirmed the 22 C target was a spawn-run temperature; OSU Extension gives 55-65 F (13-18 C) and at least 85 % RH for pinning with a 7-10 day harvest window, so the fruiting target was corrected to 18 C.

entries.name: Lion’s Mane on Hardwood
entries.notes: Hardwood sawdust or supplemented masters mix; colonise near 22-24 C, then fruit at 15-20 C and 90-95 % RH. The species is very CO2-sensitive: keeping CO2 below roughly 800 ppm holds the fruitbody compact, while stale air produces coral-like branching. Harvest when the spines are still white and 5-10 mm long, before yellowing; expect two flushes.

provenance.sourceTitle: Introduction to Fruiting — Redwood Mushroom Supply
provenance.verificationNote: The 20 C / 90 % targets sit inside the published 13-24 C fruiting range and 85-95 % RH band, and the 7-14 day maturation window supports a 12-day cycle.

entries.name: Reishi Antler/Conk
entries.notes: Hardwood sawdust blocks or logs; spawn run near 25-27 C, then primordia at 21-27 C and 90-95 % RH. Antler form is induced by elevated CO2 (above roughly 0.1 %), while a flat conk needs generous fresh air and light. Maturation takes 4-8 weeks; harvest when the white growth margin turns red, and dry thoroughly.

provenance.sourceTitle: How To Grow Reishi Mushrooms — Redwood Mushroom Supply
provenance.verificationNote: Verified 21-27 C fruiting, 85-90 % RH for development and 90-95 % at primordia, plus a 3-8 week maturation window that contains the 30-day setting.

entries.name: Enoki in Bottles
entries.notes: Commercial enoki is grown in bottles on sawdust and rice bran (4:1), colonised at 18-20 C. Fruiting drops to 10-12 C, then 3-8 C for elongation, with a collar around the neck and deliberate CO2 enrichment to keep stems long and caps small. Ready in about 10 days; only one flush per bottle.

provenance.sourceTitle: How to Grow Enoki Mushrooms at Home — Mushroom Grow Lab
provenance.verificationNote: Cross-checked 10-18 C fruiting, 85-95 % RH and a 7-14 day harvest window against the Penn State spawn-lab protocol, which drops bottles to 10-12 C then 3-8 C.

entries.name: King Trumpet on Masters Mix
entries.notes: Supplemented hardwood sawdust or masters mix in bottles or bags; colonise at 20-23 C, then cold-shock at 10 C and fruit at 13-18 C. Humidity around 85-90 % is enough — free water on stems invites bacterial blotch. Scratch the surface for even pins; harvest when caps are still slightly convex. Usually one good flush.

provenance.verificationNote: Confirmed 10-18 C fruiting, 90-95 % RH and a 10-15 day fruiting period; the stored 18 C / 85 % / 14 day values are within those bands.

entries.name: Pioppino on Supplemented Sawdust
entries.notes: Supplemented hardwood sawdust with a casing layer once colonised. Fruit at 15-20 C and 85-95 % RH with light; a 3-7 day cool period improves pinning. Caps are best picked while still rounded, before the veil opens and the gills darken. Expect two or three flushes, with the first the heaviest.

provenance.sourceTitle: How To Grow Pioppino Mushrooms — Redwood Mushroom Supply
provenance.verificationNote: The 23 C setting matched colonisation rather than fruiting; sources give 15-20 C and 80-95 % RH with harvest about 7-10 days after pins, so the target was corrected.

entries.name: Black Poplar on Straw
entries.notes: Agrocybe cylindracea is a later synonym of A. aegerita, so this is the same species as pioppino grown with a straw-based method. Aggressive on pasteurised straw; a 3-4 hour cold soak after colonisation helps synchronise pins. Fruit at 15-20 C with 85-90 % RH and good light. Harvest young; straw crops tend to be lighter but faster than sawdust.

provenance.sourceTitle: How To Grow Pioppino Mushrooms — Redwood Mushroom Supply
provenance.verificationNote: Taxonomy and climate were corrected (A. cylindracea is a synonym; fruiting is 15-20 C at 80-90 % RH), but the 18-day straw-cycle duration was not independently sourced, so the entry is not fully verified.

entries.name: Chestnut on Sawdust
entries.notes: Supplemented hardwood sawdust, often with a casing layer, colonised at 18-21 C. Fruiting needs a genuine cool shift to 13-18 C with 90-95 % RH and light for the golden scaly caps. Pins take about a week after the temperature drop and mature in 2-3 weeks. Pick before the veil breaks; expect two or three flushes.

provenance.verificationNote: Mushroom Mountain gives 50-70 F (10-21 C) and 2-3 weeks from primordia to maturity; the 21 C / 9-day setting was at the warm edge and too short, so it was corrected to 18 C / 14 days.

entries.name: Pink Oyster on Pasteurized Straw
entries.notes: Pasteurised straw, cardboard or coffee grounds; extremely fast, colonising in 7-12 days at 25-30 C. Fruiting needs 24-30 C and 85-95 % RH — below about 20 C it stalls, and colour fades with age or low light. Harvest young for best colour; 2-3 flushes in as little as three weeks.

provenance.verificationNote: Confirmed a 24-35 C fruiting range and 7-10 day fruiting at the warm end; independent culture work also puts the optimum near 28 C, matching the stored target.

entries.name: Maitake on Hardwood Blocks
entries.notes: Hardwood sawdust with bran (oak, wheat bran, millet, rye) colonises slowly, 4-8 weeks at 21-24 C. A drop to 15-20 C plus 85-90 % RH and 500-1000 lux triggers the frond clusters. Primordia take 10-14 days and the head matures over 2-3 weeks; one to two flushes, and the whole cycle runs about 12 weeks.

provenance.sourceTitle: Grifola frondosa cultivation guide — Unicorn Bags
provenance.verificationNote: Confirmed a 15-20 C optimum for fruitbody development at 85-90 % RH, with anlage formation at 10-16 C; the 10-14 day primordia-to-harvest window matches the supplier charts.

entries.name: Buna-shimeji in Bottles
entries.notes: Supplemented hardwood sawdust in bottles or bags; colonisation is slow, roughly 3-4 weeks at 20-24 C. Fruit at 13-18 C with 85-90 % RH and low light, keeping CO2 modest so stems stay short and caps firm. Clusters are ready 5-10 days after pinning; typically one or two flushes per block.

provenance.sourceTitle: The Complete Guide to Shimeji Mushrooms — GroCycle
provenance.verificationNote: Checked 13-18 C fruiting and 85-90 % RH, and a 5-10 day cluster maturation window, against GroCycle and the Penn State Hypsizygus protocol.

entries.name: Nameko in Bottles
entries.notes: Broadleaf sawdust with 10 % rice bran (15 % for conifer sawdust); colonise at 20-22 C. Unlike shiitake, do not cold-shock — step the temperature down gradually to 10-16 C and raise RH to 90-95 %. The gelatinous cap layer forms only in high humidity. Pins in 7-14 days and harvest 10-14 days later.

provenance.sourceTitle: Pholiota nameko cultivation guide — Unicorn Bags
provenance.verificationNote: Confirmed fruitbody growth from 5-20 C and about 90 % RH, with 10-14 days from initiation to harvest matching the stored 12-day window.

entries.name: Paddy Straw Mushroom in Beds
entries.notes: A true tropical species: colonise and fruit at 30-35 C with 85-95 % RH; below 25 C growth stalls and below 20 C the mycelium can die. Grow on pasteurised paddy straw or cotton waste in beds or baskets, with only moderate fresh air. First harvest comes 9-14 days after spawning; shelf life is very short, so chill immediately.

provenance.sourceTitle: How to Grow Paddy Straw Mushroom (Volvariella volvacea)
provenance.verificationNote: Confirmed the 30-35 C optimum, 85-95 % RH and 10-14 days from spawning to first harvest; the Penn State specialty-mushroom page corroborates the tropical temperature requirement.

entries.name: Button Mushroom on Compost
entries.notes: Grown on phase-II composted straw and manure, spawned at 24-25 C, then cased with peat and limestone. Airing down to 16-18 C and 85-90 % RH with CO2 under about 1000 ppm triggers pins. Harvest 15-21 days after casing, over three flushes roughly a week apart — do not let free water sit on the casing.

provenance.sourceTitle: Basic Procedures for Agaricus Mushroom Growing (Penn State Extension)
provenance.verificationNote: Confirmed harvest begins 15-21 days after casing and that cropping runs at roughly 16-18 C with 85-90 % RH, supporting the stored 17 C / 88 % / 21 day values.

entries.name: Turkey Tail on Sawdust Blocks
entries.notes: Hardwood sawdust supplemented with bran is the reliable substrate; colonise at 24-25 C for 2-4 weeks. Fruiting needs 15-21 C, 85-95 % RH, bright indirect light and strong fresh air — low oxygen produces lumpy white antlers instead of brackets. Expect a 2-4 week fruiting period; harvest the fan-shaped brackets and dry them for tea or extract.

provenance.sourceTitle: How to Grow Turkey Tail Mushrooms: A Canadian Cultivation Guide — Nature Lion
provenance.verificationNote: Confirmed 15-21 C fruiting at 85-95 % RH with a roughly two-week pin-to-bracket window; the 2-4 week total fruiting period supports the 21-day setting.
